causes.text: Swedish oat-milk maker Oatly and other plant-based beverage producers experienced surging demand as consumers shunned cow's milk for health and environmental reasons. Nielsen data cited that U.S. sales of oat milk jumped more than sevenfold to $53 million in the year to Oct. 26, 2019, while dairy sales continued to decline. The growth of Oatly and the broader vegan movement encouraged cafés to adopt nondairy milk options.

source_info.title: Starbucks launches oat milk drink as vegan movement grows

effects.text: Responding to the popularity of oat milk and plant-based diets, Starbucks announced that it would add an oat-milk latte to menus at 1,300 U.S. stores. The beverage, supplied by Oatly, became part of its U.S. lineup on Jan. 7, 2020, expanding its nondairy offerings and signalling an embrace of vegan alternatives.

source_info.title: Starbucks launches oat milk drink as vegan movement grows

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Oatly and other plant-based milk producers witnessed explosive growth as more consumers rejected cow's milk on health and environmental grounds. Reports noted that oat-milk sales surged by more than seven times during 2019, encouraging coffeehouses to experiment with nondairy beverages.

Starbucks, which had previously offered soy and almond milks, recognized that the vegan trend was driving customers toward cafes with oat-milk options. To remain competitive and appeal to sustainability-minded customers, the company negotiated a supply deal with Oatly and developed an oat-milk latte for the U.S. market.

The January 2020 launch of the oat-milk latte signalled Starbucks' strategic response to shifting consumer preferences. Investors viewed the plant-based product introduction favourably, and Starbucks' stock price ticked up about 1.5 percent in the days following the announcement, reflecting optimism that the company could capture vegan demand.

rationale: The explosive growth of Oatly and the plant-based milk category created competitive pressure on major coffee chains to offer nondairy options. By launching an oat-milk latte, Starbucks demonstrated responsiveness to consumer trends and attracted investors who saw new revenue opportunities.
counterfactual_analysis: Had Oatly not achieved such rapid growth and the vegan milk market remained niche, Starbucks would have had less incentive to expand its nondairy lineup, and its stock might not have benefited from this innovation.

adversarial_confounders.text: Beyond Meat and other plant-based meat producers were simultaneously signing deals with restaurant chains, signalling broader interest in sustainable foods.
adversarial_confounders.impact: This broader plant-based momentum could have lifted Starbucks' shares regardless of the oat-milk launch.

details.commentary: The rapid rise of brands like Oatly showed how plant-based milks were reshaping customer expectations at coffee chains. By adding an oat-milk latte to its menu, Starbucks closed a gap with competitors and independent cafes, helping defend its share among health- and sustainability-focused customers.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Regulatory and technology driven forces
details.commentary: Growing concern about health and the environmental impact of dairy made plant-based diets more popular in many markets. Starbucks' oat-milk launch showed how the company adapted its offerings to align with these broader social and ecological trends.

As more customers tried and adopted oat-milk drinks at Starbucks, early sales data encouraged management to keep promoting plant-based options. That in turn increased visibility and availability of the new beverages, reinforcing the shift in customer habits and supporting further menu innovation.
